# Talk Story Structure , narrative patterns for conference talks and lectures

Curated by Skill Harbor: narrative patterns for building conference talks and lectures that hold a room: start from where the audience is (never from a definition), connect sections with crosshead slides written as the audience's inner questions, introduce concepts in three beats, close with a call to action instead of a summary slide, and estimate timing from real per-slide rates. Includes an AI-smell checker that counts repeated heading patterns so the deck does not read as machine-written. by @minorun365, listed here with credit to its creator. Honest caveats: the skill content is written in Japanese (the patterns themselves are language-independent); it assumes you build the talk as a story told aloud, not as a handout. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via GitHub.
